newsitem.title: UK: Actinor says H2 results will be below H1.
newsitem.headline: Actinor says H2 results will be below H1.

text.p: Actinor Shipping ASA, a Norwegian shipping investment firm, said on Wednesday that its second half results will be lower than those in the first half.
"The company expects good results also for the remainder of 1997, however at a somewhat lower level than for the first half," Actinor said.
The Oslo-based firm reported first half pre-tax profits of 71 million Norwegian crowns against 59 million crowns in the first half last year.
First half operating profit fell to 94 million crowns from 98 million last time despite charter revenues increasing to 170 million crowns from 161 million.
Actinor said: "The operating profit is not directly comparable to last year as there have been considerable changes in the company's fleet."
In the first half of last year the company reported a seven million crown profit on the sale of a ship.

In the three months to the end of June pre-tax profits increased to 40 million crowns from 29 million in the same period a year earlier, helped by a sharp reduction in net financial items to five million from 21 million.
Actinor said the improvement in financial earnings was "in its entirety caused by gains from the company's share portfolio."
Interest bearing liabilities stood at US$91 million at the end of June, down $16 million from the end of last year.
Actinor said that 97.6% of shareholders had accepted the 243 crowns per share offer for the company made by Paal Wilson & Co AS and Hafslund Invest AS on June 20.

The offer valued Actinor at 965 million crowns, the company said. It made no comment on whether the company would remain listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange. --Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017
